clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: A hospitalized client has an indwelling urinary catheter. Which nursing plan best aligns with current CDC CAUTI-prevention guidance?

options.A: Confirm the catheter is still needed, maintain a closed system with unobstructed flow, and remove it promptly when no longer indicated.
options.B: Disconnect the drainage tubing each day for routine cleaning, then reconnect it after the tubing dries.
options.C: Continue the catheter for staff convenience when the client is incontinent despite no other indication.
options.D: Use routine systemic antibiotics and antiseptic periurethral cleaning to prevent bacteriuria while the catheter remains.

semantic_correction.rationale: CDC recommends urinary catheters only when needed, maintenance of a closed sterile drainage system, unobstructed urine flow, and removal as soon as the catheter is no longer needed. Prolonged catheter use is the most important CAUTI risk factor. CDC also identifies catheter use as a substitute for incontinence care as inappropriate and recommends against routine systemic antimicrobials for CAUTI prevention and against antiseptic periurethral cleaning while the catheter remains in place. Therefore option A best reflects current prevention guidance.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Prevent CAUTI by limiting indwelling catheter duration, maintaining a closed unobstructed drainage system, and removing the catheter promptly when it is no longer needed.

audit_findings_append.finding: The original answer was uniquely longest. The revised item tests catheter necessity, closed unobstructed drainage, and prompt removal without adding unsupported preventive practices.

option_audit.A: Correct. It combines the core CDC recommendations for necessity, closed drainage, unobstructed flow, and prompt removal.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Routine disconnection breaks the closed drainage system without clinical indication.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. CDC lists catheter use as a substitute for incontinence care as inappropriate when no other indication exists.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. CDC recommends against routine systemic antimicrobial prophylaxis and antiseptic periurethral cleaning for CAUTI prevention.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone follows all central CDC catheter-maintenance recommendations relevant to the scenario.
cueing_check: All four options are catheter-care plans of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
